name: Crispy Dosa with Coconut Chutney
description: Thin, golden fermented-batter crepes served with a fresh coconut and green chilli chutney.
steps: Blend the coconut, roasted chana dal, green chillies, salt and a little water into a smooth chutney.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves. When the seeds pop, pour this over the chutney.
Heat a flat pan on medium-high until a drop of water sizzles. Wipe it with an oiled cloth.
Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it outward in circles to make a thin round.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 2-3 minutes until the underside is golden and crisp.
Fold and serve hot with the chutney.
tips: The pan must be hot before you pour, or the dosa tears.
Batter that is too thick makes soft, not crisp, dosas. Thin it with a little water.
substitutions: No fresh coconut? Use 3 tbsp of roasted peanuts or extra roasted chana dal for the chutney.

name: Podi Idli
description: Soft steamed idlis tossed in a hot, fragrant tempering with idli podi.
steps: Grease the idli moulds. Pour batter into each mould.
Steam the idlis on medium heat for 10-12 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Let them rest for 2 minutes, then cut each idli into quarters.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds, and when they pop add curry leaves and asafoetida.
Add the idli pieces and idli podi. Toss on medium heat for 2-3 minutes until coated and lightly crisp at the edges.
tips: Day-old idlis work best because they stay firm when tossed.
Mix the podi with a little oil first for a smoother coating.
substitutions: No idli podi? Mix 1 tsp red chilli powder with 1 tbsp roasted chana dal powder and a pinch of salt.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: A buttery, mashed vegetable curry with pav bhaji masala, served with toasted bread rolls.
steps: Chop the potatoes, cauliflower and capsicum. Boil the potatoes, cauliflower and peas with salt for 15 minutes until very soft, then mash roughly.
Heat 2 tbsp butter in a wide pan. Add chopped onions and cook for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the capsicum and tomatoes. Cook for 6-8 minutes until the tomatoes turn mushy.
Add turmeric, chilli powder and pav bhaji masala and stir for 1 minute.
Add the mashed vegetables with 1 cup of water. Mash everything together and simmer for 10 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves. Toast the pav in the remaining butter and serve.
tips: Mashing with the back of a spoon in the pan gives the classic rough texture.
A little extra butter on top at serving makes it taste restaurant-style.
substitutions: Use oil instead of butter for a vegan bhaji, and oil on the pav.

name: Vegetable Pulao
description: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with vegetables and whole spices.
steps: Wash the rice until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a pot. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon and let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add sliced onion and green chillies. Cook for 4-5 minutes until golden.
Add the vegetables and cook for 2 minutes. Add the drained rice and gently fry for 1 minute.
Add water, salt and garam masala. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12-15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
tips: Do not stir once the lid is on or the rice turns sticky.
Use 1.75 cups of water per cup of soaked basmati.
substitutions: Frozen mixed vegetables work; add them straight to the pot.

name: Khaman Dhokla
description: Soft, spongy steamed gram flour cakes topped with a mustard and curry leaf tempering.
steps: Grease a steaming plate. Boil water in a steamer.
Whisk besan, yogurt, water, grated ginger, chopped chilli, turmeric, sugar, lemon juice and salt into a smooth, lump-free batter.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes. Add the fruit salt and 1 tsp water, stir gently once and pour into the plate immediately.
Steam covered on medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add 3 tbsp water and pour over the dhokla.
Cool for 5 minutes, cut into squares and serve.
tips: Add the fruit salt last and steam immediately, or the dhokla will not rise.
Do not over-stir after adding the fruit salt.
substitutions: No yogurt? Use 1 tbsp lemon juice and a little extra water.

name: Matar Paneer
description: Soft paneer cubes and green peas in a rich, mildly spiced tomato gravy.
steps: Blend the onions and tomatoes separately into smooth purees. Cut the paneer into cubes.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then the onion puree. Cook for 8 minutes until golden, stirring often.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt.
Cook for 8-10 minutes until the oil separates from the masala.
Add the peas and water. Simmer covered for 8 minutes.
Add the paneer, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for 3 minutes and serve.
tips: Rub the kasuri methi between your palms before adding it to release its aroma.
Soak the paneer in warm water for 10 minutes first to keep it soft.
substitutions: Use firm tofu for a vegan version; add a splash of coconut milk for richness.

name: Kadai Paneer
description: Paneer and capsicum tossed in a thick, freshly ground spice masala.
steps: Dry roast the coriander seeds, dried red chillies and half the cumin for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Crush coarsely to make the kadai masala.
Cut the paneer, capsicum and onion into large squares. Chop the tomatoes.
Heat oil, add the remaining cumin and ginger garlic paste. Fry for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 8 minutes until soft and pulpy.
Add the kadai masala, onion and capsicum. Stir on high heat for 3-4 minutes so they stay slightly crunchy.
Add the paneer, garam masala and kasuri methi. Toss for 2 minutes and garnish with coriander leaves.
tips: Keep the heat high and the vegetables chunky. That is what makes it kadai style.
Freshly crushed spices give a much stronger aroma than packaged powder.
substitutions: Use 2 tsp of coriander powder and 1 tsp red chilli powder if you cannot roast whole spices.

name: Aloo Paratha
description: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with a spiced mashed potato filling.
steps: Knead the flour with water, 1 tbsp oil and 0.5 tsp salt into a soft dough. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, peel and mash them completely with no lumps.
Mix in chopped chillies, coriander leaves, cumin, chilli powder, garam masala, amchur and the remaining salt.
Roll a dough ball into a small circle, place a spoon of filling in the centre, seal the edges and flatten gently.
Roll it out evenly with light pressure to about 15 cm across.
Cook on a hot griddle for 1-2 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden brown spots appear.
tips: Cool the potatoes fully before mixing the filling, or the dough turns soggy.
Keep the filling dry. Moist filling tears the paratha.
substitutions: Add finely grated cauliflower or paneer to the filling for variety.

name: Vegetable Biryani
description: Layered basmati rice and spiced vegetables, slow-steamed with mint and whole spices.
steps: Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes. Boil 6 cups of water with 1 tsp salt, the bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon.
Cook the rice in this water for 6-7 minutes until 70 percent done. Drain and keep aside.
Slice the onions and fry in oil for 10 minutes until deep brown. Take out half for layering.
To the pan add ginger garlic paste, tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, biryani masala and the vegetables. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add yogurt, half the mint and salt. Cook for 10 minutes until the vegetables are nearly tender and the gravy is thick.
Layer the rice over the vegetables. Top with the fried onions and the remaining mint.
Cover with a tight lid and steam on the lowest heat for 20 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before mixing gently.
tips: Parboil the rice only to 70 percent. It finishes cooking in the steam.
Seal the lid edges with dough or foil so the steam stays inside.
substitutions: No biryani masala? Use 1 tsp garam masala plus 0.5 tsp coriander powder.

name: Masoor Dal Tadka
description: Quick-cooking red lentils finished with a garlic and cumin tempering.
steps: Wash the dal and boil it with water, turmeric and salt for 15 minutes until soft and mushy. No soaking is needed.
Whisk the dal lightly to a smooth consistency.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then chopped garlic. Fry until light golden.
Add chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes. Add tomato and chilli powder and cook for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Pour the tempering into the dal, simmer for 3 minutes and garnish with coriander leaves.
tips: Skim the foam off the top as the dal boils.
Squeeze in a little lemon at the end for brightness.
substitutions: Use moong dal in place of masoor dal if you prefer.

name: Methi Thepla
description: Soft, spiced Gujarati flatbreads made with fresh fenugreek leaves and gram flour.
steps: Wash and finely chop the fenugreek leaves. Grind the ginger and green chillies into a paste.
Mix the atta, besan, fenugreek, ginger chilli paste, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, ajwain, salt, yogurt and 1 tbsp oil.
Knead into a soft dough, adding a little water as needed. Rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into small balls and roll each into a thin round.
Cook on a hot griddle for 1-2 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until brown spots appear.
tips: Roll thin so the theplas stay soft and keep well for travel.
Salt the leaves and squeeze out the moisture if they release too much water.
substitutions: Use dried fenugreek leaves (2 tbsp kasuri methi) if fresh methi is unavailable.

name: Vegetable Korma
description: Mixed vegetables in a mild, creamy coconut and cashew gravy.
steps: Blend the coconut and cashews with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat oil, add cumin, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. Add sliced onions and cook for 6-8 minutes until light golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander powder and salt and cook until soft.
Add the vegetables and water. Cover and cook for 12-15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the coconut cashew paste and simmer for 5 minutes, adding water if too thick.
tips: Do not boil hard after adding the paste, or it can split.
Keep the onions light in color for a pale, creamy korma.
substitutions: No cashews? Use 1 tbsp of poppy seeds or extra coconut.

name: Bisi Bele Bath
description: A hearty Karnataka rice, lentil and vegetable one-pot with tamarind and a signature spice powder.
steps: Wash the rice and dal together. Pressure cook with turmeric and 3 cups of water for 4-5 whistles until very soft and mushy.
Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the pulp.
In a pot boil the vegetables with 2 cups of water and salt for 10 minutes.
Add the tamarind pulp and bisi bele bath powder. Boil for 5 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the cooked rice and dal, mix well and simmer for 8-10 minutes. Add hot water for a loose, porridge-like consistency.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. Pour over the dish and serve hot.
tips: The dish thickens as it cools. Keep hot water ready to loosen it.
Serve with boondi or papad for crunch.
substitutions: No bisi bele bath powder? Use 2 tbsp sambar powder with 0.5 tsp garam masala.

name: Mixed Vegetable Sabzi
description: A simple everyday dry vegetable curry with onion, tomato and basic spices.
steps: Chop the carrot, beans and potato into small, even pieces.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then chopped onion. Cook for 4-5 minutes until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. Cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add all the vegetables and a splash of water. Mix well, cover and cook on low for 12-15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Sprinkle garam masala, mix and serve with roti.
tips: Cut the vegetables the same size so they cook evenly.
Add the peas in the last 8 minutes to keep them bright.
substitutions: Use any seasonal vegetables such as cabbage, capsicum or cauliflower.

name: Curd Rice
description: Cool, creamy rice mixed with yogurt and finished with a mustard seed tempering.
steps: Mash the warm rice lightly with the back of a spoon so it turns soft and creamy. Let it cool.
Mix in the yogurt, milk and salt until smooth.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and when they pop add chopped chilli, grated ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Pour the tempering over the rice and mix. Garnish with coriander leaves.
Chill for 15 minutes if you like it cold.
tips: Mix the yogurt in after the rice has cooled, or it turns sour fast.
Add a little milk before serving if it thickens in the fridge.
substitutions: Add grated carrot or pomegranate seeds for sweetness and crunch.

name: Sabudana Khichdi
description: Soft sago pearls stir-fried with potato, peanuts and green chilli, a fasting-day favourite.
steps: Rinse the sabudana until the water runs clear. Soak it in just enough water to cover for 6-8 hours, until the pearls squash easily between your fingers. Drain fully.
Dry roast the peanuts until crisp, cool and coarsely crush them. Mix with the sabudana, salt and sugar.
Boil, peel and cube the potato.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds and chopped green chillies. Add the potato and fry for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Add the sabudana mixture and stir gently on medium-low heat for 4-5 minutes until the pearls turn translucent.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves.
tips: Do not over-soak or add too much water. The pearls should stay separate, not sticky.
Stir gently so the pearls do not break.
substitutions: Use rock salt if you are fasting.
